author: BBC News
description:
British PM Andy Burnham has said the UK has lost more than it has gained from leaving the European Union in a speech ahead of a UK-EU summit later this week.

Speaking at the Lord Mayor's Banquet in London, Andy Burnham compared the UK's Brexit deal to the "emperor's new clothes" - saying "a needlessly hard Brexit" had created barriers for businesses and the promise to "take back control" was not delivered.

He is due to sign new agreements on food, energy and youth mobility with the bloc at the summit, after the substance of those deals was set by his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

The opposition Conservatives have said Labour are "dragging us into the European Union via the back door".

In his first major speech on foreign policy, the prime minister said that following the summit he would begin new discussions with the EU about options for "our long-term relationship".  However, he warned it would take time and insisted that "at every stage the British people will be the boss".  Bur
title: “Brexit hasn’t worked and Britain lost more that it gained” says Andy Burnham | BBC News

description:
The UK, Australia, Canada and Italy have issued a joint statement urging Israel to "allow immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza", where they say the situation on the ground is "dire" as winter closes in. This comes after heavy rains flooded thousands of shelters and caused a deadly landslide. 

Last week, President Donald Trump's Board of Peace issued a rare criticism of Israel, saying its response to the situation in Gaza "remains insufficient". And the European Union issued a similar statement on Saturday, expressing concern over what it called Gaza's "persistent and devastating humanitarian crisis".

The Israeli military authority which controls the Gaza crossings has said it is co-ordinating with the Board of Peace and the UN on a winter plan, and that 93,000 tents and 8,600 aid trucks with winter supplies had entered the territory. It added that reconstruction "can only begin after Hamas fully disarms".

description:
Warning: Distressing details of death and injury and discussion of suicide.
 
A prominent expert in forensic medicine, Michael Freeman, who says he has reviewed Jeffrey Epstein's autopsy records, has told BBC Newsnight that he believes Epstein's death in prison was the result of homicide. 
 
Freeman contends that Epstein was assaulted and strangled, most likely from behind. 
 
Dr Barbara Sampson, Chief Medical Examiner of New York City at the time of Epstein's autopsy, who ruled that Epstein's death was a suicide, has previously said: "I stand firmly behind our determination of the cause and manner of death for Mr. Epstein. The cause is hanging, the manner is suicide". The BBC has approached Dr Barbara Sampson for comment.
 
Newsnight is the BBC's flagship news and current affairs TV programme - with analysis, debate, exclusives, and robust interviews.
title: Epstein death "result of a homicide", claims forensic medicine expert | BBC News

Robert Pattinson has been announced as the seventh person to play Bond in the official film series.
 
In a statement, the 40-year-old British actor says "to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime".
 
Speculation about Daniel Craig's replacement has been rife, with actors including Josh O'Connor, Callum Turner and Jack Lowden thought to have made it to the final screen tests.

Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight has been writing the script for the next film, with Dune's Denis Villeneuve to direct.
Thanking those who auditioned, Villeneuve says "we were surrounded by extraordinary talent", adding Pattinson "brings a spirit that is completely new".

author: BBC News
description:
Thousands of school pupils in England are missing more than half the academic year.

The latest figures published by the government in October show that 168,000 pupils (2.32%) were classed as severely absent in the 2025/2026 autumn and spring terms.

Back in spring 2019, this figure was under 60,000.

Children who miss school are more at risk of becoming a Neet - not in employment, education or training, according to experts.

A government-commissioned review into how to solve the problem of nearly one million young people being Neet is due to be published on Tuesday.

BBC News journalist Gemma Roper has spoken to teenagers who do not go to school and those who are trying to fix the issue.

Mia Latter alleges that she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 - she has waived her right to anonymity and says she is campaigning for a staggered age of consent in an interview with the Sunday Times.
 
She was one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation. Brand denied the allegations at the time.
 
Latter said it was "disgusting" that a culture existed in the 2000s that "normalised and celebrated" celebrities having relationships with teenagers.
 
Brand has been sentenced to 10-and-a-half years for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. None of the women in the 2023 media investigation were complainants in Brand's recent criminal trial.

description:
What happens when humans create powerful but dangerous technologies?

This week we’re introducing The Global Backstory, the new strand of our show that explores the history behind the news today. We constantly hear stories about artificial intelligence, but most of them are about where AI is going; in this five-episode series we’re looking at where it came from.

The rise of AI is often compared with the dawn of the nuclear age because of its epoch-changing nature. So, what lessons does history offer about how we might face the dangers – and the opportunities – that arise from this revolutionary technology? 

In this first episode we speak to the history podcaster and author Dan Carlin about what the past does and doesn’t teach us about our future.

A crucial US satellite internet service is still operating too slowly and affecting Ukraine's ability to stop Russian attacks, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
 
"We are counting on these restrictions being lifted. The protection of lives and Ukraine's energy infrastructure ahead of winter directly depends on this," he said.
 
The issue over the speed of the Starshield system - a military-grade service developed by Elon Musk's Starlink and provided to Ukraine by the US government - has been rumbling on for weeks.
 
Meanwhile, the Duke of Sussex has met injured war veterans in a surprise visit to Ukraine.
